takeaway: Long-term GORD refluxes acid into the distal oesophagus. Chronic inflammation causes metaplasia: one differentiated cell type replaced by another. It is reversible if the irritant is removed.

question.text: Endoscopy of a patient with long-term GORD shows erythema around the distal third of the oesophagus. Which pathological process has most likely occurred?

lines.text: In gastro-oesophageal reflux disease, the stomach refluxes acid up into the oesophagus.
The distal oesophagus becomes red and inflamed.
If the exposure is severe and chronic enough, the lining changes.
One differentiated cell type is replaced by another. That is metaplasia.
The process is reversible: if the irritant is removed, the tissue may return to normal.
Neoplasia and dysplasia are not the most likely process here.
